channel.title: Speak Like Yourself: Brazilian Portuguese blog
channel.description: Real Brazilian Portuguese: survival phrases, slang, pronunciation and honest learning guides, by Rafael.

item.title: How to Be Polite in Brazilian Portuguese (Desculpa, Com Licenca, Por Favor)
item.description: Learn the real difference between desculpa and com licenca so you stop apologizing when you only need to pass by.

item.title: How to Say What You Like in Brazilian Portuguese (Gostar De)
item.description: Master gostar de, its de + article contractions, and how to talk about actions you enjoy with real example sentences.

item.title: O or A? Noun Gender in Brazilian Portuguese Made Simple
item.description: Learn the trick that predicts masculine or feminine almost every time, plus the small exception groups worth memorizing early.

item.title: Ficar: The Most Useful Verb Brazilians Use Every Day
item.description: Ficar means "to stay," but also "to become," "to be located" and even "to hook up." See fica, ficou and ficar com in real examples.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese Past Tense: How to Talk About What You Did
item.description: Learn the one tense that lets you narrate a whole day, plus the five irregular verbs you'll reach for constantly, and the trick that keeps stories from sounding flat.

item.title: The LH and NH Sounds: How to Pronounce Filho and Banho (with audio)
item.description: Master the tongue position behind these tricky letter pairs so filho and banho stop sounding forced.

item.title: Ser vs Estar: The Two Ways to Say 'To Be' in Brazilian Portuguese
item.description: Learn one simple test to instantly pick the right verb, plus the pairs where the same word changes meaning depending on which one you use.

item.title: Voce or Tu? How Brazilians Really Say 'You'
item.description: Você means "you," and it is the everyday default across most of Brazil. See where tu takes over, and which one sounds natural where you are going.

item.title: The Easy Brazilian Future: Just Use Vou + a Verb
item.description: How to talk about the future in Brazilian Portuguese with 'vou' + a verb, when Brazilians skip the formal future entirely, and the few times it still shows up.

item.title: Bora? How Brazilians Make Plans and Invitations
item.description: The words Brazilians actually use to suggest, invite, and lock in plans, from 'bora' to 'fica pra depois', plus natural ways to say yes or bail out.

item.title: Te Amo or Amo-te? Object Pronouns Brazilians Actually Use
item.description: Where object pronouns really land in spoken Brazilian Portuguese, why 'te amo' beats 'amo-te', and how to place me, te, and o without sounding like a textbook.

item.title: Por Que, Porque, Por Quê and Porquê: The Four Porques Made Simple
item.description: A clear breakdown of the four porques, when each one appears, and examples that make the spelling choice feel less random.

item.title: How to Ask Questions in Brazilian Portuguese (Que, Qual, Quando, Onde)
item.description: A simple guide to que, qual, quando and onde, with question patterns, examples, and the mistakes beginners usually make.

item.title: Brazilian Filler Words: Né, Tipo, Nossa and Sounding Natural
item.description: A practical guide to né, tipo, nossa and other fillers that make Brazilian Portuguese sound more natural in real conversation.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese Diminutives: Why -inho and -inha Are Everywhere
item.description: -inho and -inha make a word smaller, sweeter or friendlier: cafezinho, amorzinho, pouquinho. Here is what each ending signals and when it sounds childish.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese Mini Dialogues for Real Life
item.description: Short, ready-to-use exchanges for greetings, ordering, asking for help, and keeping a simple conversation going.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese False Friends: Words That Trick English Speakers
item.description: The words that look familiar to English speakers but mean something else entirely, with the real meanings and how to dodge the awkward mix-ups.

item.title: How Brazilians Text: WhatsApp Slang & Abbreviations (kkk, vc, tb)
item.description: kkk is how Brazilians laugh in text, vc means você and tb means também. Decode the rest of the group-chat shorthand before you reply.

item.title: Days, Months & Telling Time in Brazilian Portuguese
item.description: Full reference tables, how dates are written and said, and the small habits that trip beginners up when telling time.

item.title: Learn Portuguese With Music: 15 Brazilian Songs for Beginners
item.description: Use Brazilian songs as real study material, with beginner-friendly picks and a simple method for turning lyrics into practice.

item.title: How to Immerse Yourself in Portuguese Without Leaving Home
item.description: Build a home immersion routine with phone settings, Brazilian creators, music, shows, podcasts, and small thinking habits.

item.title: Duolingo for Portuguese: Does It Actually Work?
item.description: An honest look at what the app gets right, where it quietly leaves you stuck, and what to pair it with so you actually speak.

item.title: Best Way to Learn Brazilian Portuguese in 2026: Apps vs Tutors vs Self-Study
item.description: Compare apps, tutors and self-study honestly, then build the mix that gives you daily habit, real input and useful feedback.

item.title: How to Learn Brazilian Portuguese by Yourself (Self-Study Guide)
item.description: A self-study system built on input, output and feedback, with a daily routine, the right tools, and how to push past plateaus.

item.title: Why 'de' Sounds Like 'jee': Palatalization Made Simple
item.description: The simple sound rule behind 'jee' and 'chee', with audio and the one habit that quietly upgrades your accent.

item.title: The Brazilian R: When It Sounds Like an H
item.description: Yes, Brazilians often say R like an English H, so Rio sounds like "HEE-oo." Learn exactly when it happens, when R taps instead, and how to tell.

item.title: How to Pronounce the Nasal Sounds (ão, ãe, õe)
item.description: A step-by-step way into the sound that gives most beginners away, with audio so you can match it out loud.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese Pronunciation Guide (with Audio)
item.description: Hear the sounds English speakers usually miss, from nasal vowels to the Brazilian R, and copy them with cleaner, more confident rhythm.

item.title: Brazilian Terms of Endearment: What Meu Bem, Amor and Benzinho Mean
item.description: Meu bem means "my good" and lands like "sweetheart" or "darling." See when Brazilians say it, plus amor and benzinho, and who you can safely call it.

item.title: Beleza, Legal, Massa: How Brazilians Really Say 'Cool'
item.description: Beleza means beauty, but in Brazil it mostly means "cool," "OK" or "all good." See when to say beleza, legal or massa so you sound natural.

item.title: What Does 'Saudade' Really Mean? (The Untranslatable Word)
item.description: Saudade is the ache of missing someone or something you love. See how Brazilians use it in real sentences, like "estou com saudade" and "saudades de você."

item.title: Brazilian Slang: 50 Gírias to Sound Like a Native
item.description: Fifty everyday gírias with what they actually mean, when each one fits, and how to drop them without sounding like you swallowed a textbook.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese for the Airport & Getting Around
item.description: Immigration, taxis and apps, buses and directions, with real phrases you can pull up and use the moment you land.

item.title: Brazilian Portuguese Greetings: Say Hello Like a Local
item.description: Real ways to say hi for morning, night, texting and meeting people, with pronunciation and the cultural cues that come with them.

item.title: 101 Brazilian Portuguese Phrases for Travelers
item.description: Greetings, directions, restaurants, shopping and emergencies covered in one pack, with pronunciation and audio samples to copy.

item.title: How Long Does It Really Take to Learn Brazilian Portuguese?
item.description: Honest timelines by level, the hours it takes, the habits that speed things up, and what conversational actually means.

item.title: European vs Brazilian Portuguese: Which Should You Learn?
item.description: The real differences in accent, vocabulary and grammar between the two, and a clear way to decide which one fits your goals.

item.title: Is Brazilian Portuguese Hard to Learn? An Honest Answer
item.description: Short answer: easier than you think in most ways, tricky in three. See what carries over from English, what does not, and how to make it manageable.

item.title: How to Learn Brazilian Portuguese: A Beginner's Roadmap (2026)
item.description: An honest, step-by-step roadmap for 2026: what to do first, what to skip, and how long fluency really takes.

item.title: Portuguese Numbers 1-100, Prices & Phone Numbers (with Audio)
item.description: Count to 100 and on to 1,000, then hear how Brazilians actually say prices in reais, read out phone numbers with meia, and say dates.

item.title: How to Order Food in Brazil: Restaurant Portuguese
item.description: Get a table, order dishes and drinks, handle dietary needs and pay, with real phrases and the cultural tips that smooth it over.
